# Story 24 — agent: empty, loading and error states are designed, not accidental (Story: CRM-31)

## Prerequisites

- **PLATFORM-12-WEB completed** — the desk shell exists (`web/src/app/desk-shell/DeskShell.tsx`). This story adds primitives the shell and later screens will use.
- **`LANGUAGES-1-WEB` (CRM-35) built the hardcoded-strings guard and `PLATFORM-12-WEB` (CRM-27) widened it** — `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` currently scans `['pages', 'features', 'app']`. (The generated plan credited CRM-28, which is the CI story; corrected in review.) Any decision this story makes about where the primitives live must reconcile with that scan.
- Coordinate with the owner of `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts` (`ApiErrorCode` union) — this story consumes it exhaustively; adding a ninth code must not slip past `tsc -b`.
- **Read first:** `.squad/plan-lessons.md` (rules L-6 — hardcoded-string scan holes, and L-15 — vitest does not typecheck, `npm run build` is the proof).

---

## Story Goal

Ship three shared UI primitives — **empty**, **error**, **loading (skeleton)** — that any web screen renders when it needs to express one of the four `useRequest` statuses (`idle`, `loading`, `success`, `error`). Move sign-in's ad-hoc `messageFor(code, t)` switch into a single shared, exhaustively-typed error-message map keyed by `ApiErrorCode`. Register all sentences in both `en` and `ar` resource files so `defineLocale`'s missing/extra-keys check enforces them in lockstep. Make it typecheck-hard to add a new `ApiErrorCode` without adding its message.

Out of scope (from intake, restate for the executor):
- No real desk screen changes beyond sign-in's message wiring.
- No changes to `useRequest`'s status union, `ApiError` shape, or `ApiErrorCode` union.
- No language switching, no locale date/number formatting, no 401 redirect behaviour.
- No `api/` or `android/` change. No new dependency.

## Product rules (from story)

Current: sign-in owns its own `messageFor` switch; there are no shared empty/error/loading primitives.
New:
- One shared error-message map keyed exhaustively by `ApiErrorCode`.
- Three shared primitives: `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `SkeletonBlock` (name TBD in § 2), rendered by screens off the `useRequest` status.
- Loading state reserves the same shape as the content it becomes — **no layout jump**.
- Every colour used by any new primitive is a `--` token in `tokens.css`.

## Frontend Tasks

_No backend changes required. No `android/` changes. No new dependency._

### 1 — Shared error-message map keyed by `ApiErrorCode`

**Create file:** `web/src/shared/api/error-messages.ts`

- Import `ApiErrorCode` from `./errors`.
- Import the translator type from `web/src/shared/i18n` (whatever `useT()` / `defineLocale` returns; match the shape sign-in uses today).
- Export:

  **Corrected in review — this translator is an object, not a function.**
  `useTranslation()` returns `{ language, t, dir }` where `t` is the whole
  `Messages` tree and a screen reads `t.signIn.heading`. There is no `t('…')`
  call form and no exported type named `T`; the type is `Messages`, exported
  from `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`.

  Given that, the simplest exhaustive shape is not a separate map of functions
  at all — it is a section of the locale, typed to be exhaustive:

  ```ts
  // in web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts, inside the exported object
  errors: {
    BAD_REQUEST: '…',
    UNAUTHENTICATED: '…',
    FORBIDDEN: '…',
    NOT_FOUND: '…',
    CONFLICT: '…',
    VALIDATION_FAILED: '…',
    RATE_LIMITED: '…',
    INTERNAL: '…',
  } satisfies Record<ApiErrorCode, string>,
  ```

  `satisfies Record<ApiErrorCode, string>` makes `tsc -b` fail the moment a
  ninth code joins the union without a sentence, and `defineLocale` already
  fails when `ar.ts` is missing one or carries an extra. Two guarantees, no new
  file, and the lookup at a call site is `t.errors[error.code]`.

  Only add `web/src/shared/api/error-messages.ts` if something genuinely cannot
  live in the locale — and say what.

For each primitive, follow the `Card.tsx` + `Card.css` pattern already in `web/src/shared/ui/`. Each takes its text via props/children so the file itself has **no** string literals (this is the answer to the L-6 hole — primitives are literal-free; the sentences live in `shared/i18n`, which `defineLocale` already enforces in lockstep).

**Create files:**

- `web/src/shared/ui/EmptyState.tsx` + `EmptyState.css`

  Props: `title: ReactNode`, `body?: ReactNode`, `action?: ReactNode` (the "next action" button provided by the caller). Renders a `Card`-shaped block using existing tokens.

- `web/src/shared/ui/ErrorState.tsx` + `ErrorState.css`

  Props: `title: ReactNode`, `body: ReactNode` (the sentence from `errorMessageFor`), `onRetry?: () => void`, `retryLabel?: ReactNode`. When `onRetry` is set, render a retry `Button`.

- `web/src/shared/ui/SkeletonBlock.tsx` + `SkeletonBlock.css`

  Props: `height?: string`, `width?: string`, `radius?: string`, `count?: number`. The css **reserves the shape** of the content that is coming; add a `/* Reserving the shape here so the page does not jump when success arrives — do not simplify to a spinner. */` comment above the rule. The shimmer uses tokens from `tokens.css` only.

**Update file:** `web/src/shared/ui/index.ts` — re-export the three new primitives alongside the existing ones. Match the current export style.

**Update file:** `web/src/shared/ui/tokens.css` — add tokens for any new colour used by `SkeletonBlock` (e.g. `--color-skeleton-base`, `--color-skeleton-shimmer`). No colour literal may live outside this file (D-1 is enforced by `tokens.test.ts`).

### 3 — i18n sentences in both languages

**Update files:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

- Under an `errors` group, add one key per `ApiErrorCode` value (mirror the code names from `errors.ts`). The English sentences are the ones currently produced by `messageFor` in `SignInPage.tsx` — copy them **verbatim** to preserve today's sign-in output.
- Under a `states` group, add the placeholder sentences the primitives read when a caller does not supply its own (or leave the primitives text-agnostic and register only what the current sign-in call site actually needs — pick one and be explicit; do not add unused keys).
- `defineLocale` enforces missing/extra key parity between `en` and `ar` in lockstep; that is the mechanism that makes forgetting an Arabic translation fail the build.

### 4 — Sign-in keeps its own sentences, and that is the point

**Do not** delete `messageFor` from `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` and
route it through the shared map. **The intake asked for that and the intake was
wrong** — this is the correction.

Sign-in's mapper is not an ad-hoc copy of a generic one. It exists because
IDENTITY-1-API deliberately answers **401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` for a wrong
password, an unknown address and a disabled account alike**, so that the
response is not a directory of who works here — and the screen has to keep that
promise. `t.signIn.errorUnauthenticated` is "That email and password do not
match an account", one sentence covering three different truths on purpose.

A generic `UNAUTHENTICATED` sentence is about a session that ended, which is
what every *other* screen means by that code. One map cannot say both. Forcing
sign-in onto the shared map would either leak the distinction the API refuses to
make, or drag sign-in's deliberate vagueness onto screens where it is merely
unhelpful.

So:

- The shared map carries the **generic** meaning of each documented code, for
  any screen whose load failed.
- `SignInPage` keeps `messageFor` **unchanged**, and gains a comment saying why
  it is not using the shared map, naming the API's one-refusal rule and the
  story that set it. Without that comment the next reader deletes it as
  duplication — which is exactly what this plan nearly did.
- `SignInPage.test.tsx` is not touched at all.

### 5 — Hardcoded-strings guard reconciliation (L-6)

**Update file:** `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`

- The primitives take their sentences via props, so their files contain no user-visible literals. The sentences live in `shared/i18n`, which `defineLocale` covers.
- **Corrected in review — widen the scan.** The generated plan chose to leave
  the roots alone and add a comment saying a reviewer should widen them if a
  primitive ever bakes in a literal, and its own edge-case table admits the case
  would be "caught only by review… if this happens twice, widen the scan". That
  is the L-6 shape with the hole documented instead of closed, and CRM-27 closed
  exactly this hole two stories ago.
- `shared/ui` is already free of user-facing literals — every primitive takes
  its text as props — so widening costs nothing today and stops the question
  being asked again:

  ```ts
  const SCANNED = ['pages', 'features', 'app', 'shared/ui'];
  ```

- Prove it (L-16): put a literal in one of the new primitives, watch the suite
  name the file, remove it.

### 6 — Fourth criterion: the review affordance

Per the intake, do **not** invent a weak mechanical guard that pretends to enforce "every screen has all three states". The enforcement is:

1. `useRequest` is the only status source (already true).
2. The three primitives are the easiest thing to reach for.
3. Review can point at each primitive by name in a diff.

Add a short note to `docs/architecture.md` (a single paragraph under the existing web section) naming the three primitives and stating that a screen using `useRequest` should render each of them for its `loading`, `error`, and empty-`success` branches. **Do not** restate anything already in taxonomy or architecture; add one paragraph and link out.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **New `ApiErrorCode` added to the union but no message registered** — `tsc -b` fails at `web/src/shared/api/error-messages.ts` because `Record<ApiErrorCode, …>` requires every arm. Verified by `npm run build` (L-15: vitest does not typecheck).
- **New `errors.<code>` key added to `en.ts` but not `ar.ts` (or vice versa)** — `defineLocale` in `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` fails with a missing/extra key error. Same mechanism sign-in relies on today.
- **A colour literal sneaks into `SkeletonBlock.css`** — `web/src/shared/ui/tokens.test.ts` scans `web/src` and fails (D-1).
- **A primitive file gains a user-visible literal** — the current scan does not cover `shared/ui/`; caught only by review. The comment added in § 5 is the guardrail. If this happens twice, widen the scan.
- **Loading is a spinner instead of a skeleton** — allowed by types, forbidden by the design comment in `SkeletonBlock.css`. Caught in review.
- **Sign-in's rendered sentences change** — caught by `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.test.tsx` (unchanged assertions).
- **RTL layout** — primitives use existing `Stack` / logical CSS properties as the current primitives do; verify `ar` locale shape matches `en` in `primitives.test.tsx` style.
- **A caller forgets `onRetry`** — `ErrorState` renders no button; that is the documented shape. Caller decides whether retry applies.
